newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares shrug off weak Wall St, banks lead.
newsitem.headline: German shares shrug off weak Wall St, banks lead.

text.p: German shares shrugged off weakness on Wall Street on Wednesday amid a wave of interest in banking and auto industry shares.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks after-bourse dealings in the 30-share blue chip shares, ended the day up 64.29 at 3,439.22, topping the mid-afternoon DAX bourse close of 3,418.12. June DTB DAX futures closed up 61 at 3,455.

Banks were at the centre of market attention as dealers said the recent Krupp-Thyssen affair had caused a renewal of merger speculation in the financial sector and as Deutsche Bank, the largest German bank, detailed its 1996 results.
And Daimler-Benz AG hit a new all-time high in late trade after reporting a convincing return to profits in 1996 after 1995's unprecedented loss.
Deutsche Bank ended the day up 98 pfennigs at 92.90 after it detailed 1996 data and said it was optimistic for 1997.

Dresdner Bank and Commerzbank, the second and third largest in the sector, also rose amid significant volumes, while the highest gains were seen in the shares of Hypo-Bank, which ended the day up six percent at 58.26 marks as traders said was being viewed as a potential takeover target.
Dresdner, which has no notifiable stake in the mortgage specialist which is Germany's fifth largest bank, was being mooted as being interested in Hypo-Bank, a rumour on which it declined comment.
Meanwhile Daimler ended the day up 4.5 percent at 135.80 marks after announcing 1996 net profit of 2.8 billion marks.
"Those were huge numbers," remarked one dealer, noting that the release of the data was wholly unexpected.
Meanwhile rival BMW rose 5.9 percent to 327 marks on continued positive reaction to more 1996 business details given at a news conference on Tuesday.

Utility Veba fell 1.42 marks to 98.28 marks in IBIS after its 1996 results, which showed a group pre-tax profit rose 16 percent to 4.44 billion marks. It said however that future earnings growth was likely to be slower.

Steel and engineering group Thyssen managed to pull back most of early losses made on a continued reaction to the cancelled takeover bid by Krupp, which is due to make way for a steel joint venture between the two.
Thyssen shares ended just 50 pfennigs down at 374.50 marks in IBIS trade after earlier hitting a low of 367.50.
